394: Enablement of the Storer provisional application for the interference count; the Board found the S1 provisional together with prior art did not enable the 2'F(down) compounds without undue experimentation, and the court affirmed.
1193: Denial of JMOL of no enablement; Appellants not entitled to JMOL.
We therefore reject Appellants’ arguments and conclude that Appellants are not entitled to JMOL of no written description and no enablement.
1554: Enablement: court reaffirmed its earlier holding that the asserted claims of four Promega patents are invalid for lack of enablement.
We reaffirm our holdings on the enablement, licensing, and active inducement issues.
1655: Enablement of the disparate-databases claims in the MicroStrategy and TIBCO suits: the court held genuine issues of material fact preclude summary judgment of non-enablement, reversing the grants of summary judgment of invalidity.
Accordingly, we reverse the district court's grants of summary judgment that the asserted claims are invalid for lack of enablement.
1709: Whether the PMA reference is enabling as prior art, so that it can anticipate, and whether using it would require undue experimentation
the Board's conclusion that the PMA reference is enabling is correct.
1961: Whether Tsien enables a skilled artisan to make the base-labeled 3'-OH-capped nucleotide without undue experimentation, so that Tsien can serve as an anticipating reference. Court rejected the non-enablement argument.
if novel and nonobvious chemistry was needed to practice the claimed inventions, Dr. Ju would have been obligated to disclose this chemistry in the patent.
1967: Whether the tribunal properly rejected Dow's enablement defense (monocot coverage); challenge rejected.
The same is true of Dow's challenge to the tribunal's rejection of its enablement defense.
2173: Enablement of the Counts and pending claims by the Beachy priority applications.
We also affirm the PTAB's determination that both the Counts and all the pending claims of the '121 and '934 applications are sufficiently described and enabled by the Beachy priority applications.
3350: Whether Magnusson is an enabling prior art reference for claims 1 and 8; court held it enabling, so the Board's determination was affirmed.
We therefore conclude that Magnusson is an enabling reference with respect to claims 1 and 8 and affirm the Board's holding that these claims are anticipated.
3503: Enablement of asserted claims challenged by Lupin: not invalid for lack of enablement
We agree with Allergan that the asserted claims are not invalid for lack of enablement.
3769: Enablement of the asserted claims of the '180 and '405 patents under 35 U.S.C. §112(a); claims held not enabled across the full scope.
we affirm the district court's grant of summary judgment that the asserted claims of the ʼ180 patent and the ʼ405 patent are invalid for lack of enablement.
3821: Enablement of a design patent claim disclosed by a single two-dimensional plan-view drawing of a shoe bottom; the Board found the claim not enabled and the court reversed.

Because a designer of ordinary skill in the art, judging Maatita's design as would an ordinary observer, could make comparisons for infringement purposes based on the provided, two-dimensional depiction, Maatita's claim meets the enablement and definiteness requirements of § 112.
4393: Enablement of the '860 application claims under pre-AIA §112 ¶1: whether the specification enables simulation across all modes of operation
No reasonable factfinder could conclude that the '860 application meets the enablement requirement.
4449: Enablement under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112 para. 1 for claims 33 and 34 (artificial glands with membranes of cellular components); Board rejection affirmed because creating the glands would require undue experimentation.
The Board did not err in concluding that creating the artificial glands covered by claims 33 and 34 would require undue experimentation.
4683: Enablement of the '597 patent claims: majority held claims not enabled under Wands factors, affirming JMOL of invalidity
we conclude as a matter of law that the '597 patent is invalid for lack of enablement.
4799: Whether the prior art references (Barger/Dessaignes) are enabling, i.e., whether a skilled artisan could make creatine nitrate from the disclosures without undue experimentation; the court held the prior art enabled and any burden-standard error harmless.
Based on the record of this case, we conclude that it is.
4813: Remaining independent claims 19 and 27 (and dependents) were held not enabled because they do not cure the lack of enablement of the term 'object routing' identified in JPMorgan.
For claims 19 and 27, none of the claimed steps therein describe what object routing is or how it is accomplished.
5354: Enablement of the full scope of claim 1's 'first set of rules' limitation; summary judgment of nonenablement invalidity vacated because the Developers did not identify concrete unenabled embodiments within claim scope.
We do not go so far as to hold that there is a triable issue of fact on enablement—instead, we vacate the judgment and remand for the district court to consider how to proceed.
5770: Enablement under §112(a): the claimed inventions were held not enabled, as affirmed in Swartz II and applied through collateral estoppel and the Board's rejection.
Substantially identical claims were previously found to be invalid as lacking utility and not enabled.
6411: Enablement of claim 19 of the '738 patent: claim not enabled as a matter of law because the full scope (monocrystalline growth layer directly on amorphous buffer layer) was not enabled
We conclude that claim 19 is not enabled as a matter of law and therefore reverse the district court's denial of Defendants' motion for JMOL on this issue.
7173: Enablement not reached; court declined to decide enablement for first time on appeal
in this case we decline to reach the question of enablement for the first time on appeal
7407: Enablement of the '430 patent over Ariosa's challenge that it does not enable the full scope of claim 1 for targeted sequencing
We therefore affirm the jury's verdict regarding enablement and the district court's subsequent denial of Ariosa's motion for JMOL.
7531: Enablement of claim 2 of the '090 patent; district court found enabled, affirmed.
We discern no error in that conclusion.
7635: Enablement of proposed amended claims despite an admitted typographical error in the specification (step 168 vs. step 176).
The Board did not err in determining that the proposed amended claims were enabled, despite an admitted error in the specification
7933: Enablement of prior art reference: Board erred by shifting to the petitioner the burden to prove the prior art (Konno) was enabling; the patentee bears the burden of nonenablement. Error held harmless.
Thus, regardless of the forum, prior art patents and publications enjoy a presumption of enablement, and the patentee/applicant has the burden to prove nonenablement for such prior art.
8286: Whether Tolman's single-line system is enabled; prior art publications presumed enabling, so the challenge was rejected

prior art published patent applications are presumed enabling and Cameron does not present any evidence or meaningful argument as to why a skilled artisan could not make and use Tolman's disclosed single-line system.
8510: Enablement under 112(a): the Board affirmed the rejection of claims 1-22 as lacking enablement because the specification does not enable the full scope of the claims without undue experimentation (Wands factors).
Accordingly, we affirm the Board's rejection of claims 1–22 as lacking enablement under § 112(a).
8512: Enablement of functionally defined antibody claims ('165 patent claims 19 and 29 and '741 patent claim 7); district court JMOL of lack of enablement affirmed under Wands factors
We therefore conclude that, after weighing the Wands factors, the court did not err in concluding that undue experimentation would be required to practice the full scope of these claims.
8759: Enablement of claims 1-4, 19, and 20 of the '590 patent over the full scope of claimed antibodies; summary judgment of lack of enablement affirmed
we hold the '590 patent fails to teach skilled artisans how to make and use the full scope of claimed antibodies without unreasonable experimentation.
8791: Enablement of the asserted claims of the '400 and '323 patents; jury verdict of non-enablement upheld on JMOL

We therefore conclude that there was ample evidence to support a finding that, before the 2009 priority date of the '400 and '323 patents, relevant artisans did not know how to perform nanopore sequencing for more than a narrow range of the full scope of nucleic acids covered by the asserted claims.
8967: Enablement of the full scope of claims (non-random lysine PEGylation at the B-domain): jury verdict of enablement upheld, favoring the patent owner.
we conclude that substantial evidence supports the jury's verdict that Baxalta failed to prove by clear and convincing evidence that the asserted claims are invalid for lack of enablement.
9593: Enablement: the Board found the full scope of the substitute claims not enabled under the Wands factors; the court affirmed.
We see no error in the Board's factual findings and discern no legal error in its determination of lack of enablement for the substitute claims.
9871: Enablement rejection under §112(a) of the four applications; the court held the experimental data inadequate and affirmed the Board's finding that the claims were not enabled.
The Board applied a reasonable and objective standard, and acted reasonably in sustaining the examiners' requirements.
10496: Enablement of open-ended density claims ('320 claims 1 and 3; '456 claims 11, 12, 15, 16, 21): the Commission found the claims enabled because they have an inherent upper limit of about 144 connections per U space that the specification enables skilled artisans to approach; affirmed under substantial evidence review.
We therefore affirm the Commission's enablement determination.
10938: Enablement of '793 patent claims as construed by the district court.
We agree with United Therapeutics that the claims are adequately enabled as they were construed by the district court.
11362: Enablement of claim 1 of the '956 patent: claimed method allegedly impossible to perform, so not enabled. Court held claim not invalid for lack of enablement.
Hence, the district court did not err in failing to find claim 1 of the '956 patent invalid due to indefiniteness or lack of enablement.
11445: Enablement of substitute claim 32 and its parent claim 24 (no 'top flanges' required); court affirmed Board that claim 32 was enabled.
We see no reversible error in those determinations or in the Board's rejection of the enablement challenge to substitute claim 32.
11876: Enablement of claims 1-6 and 23 of the '141 patent as to non-carbon-block filters; Commission found undue experimentation required and claims nonenabled; affirmed.
The record thus supports the Commission's legal conclusion that the '141 patent required undue experimentation to enable the full scope of the asserted claims.
12130: Enablement under §112(a): whether the asserted claims are enabled without undue experimentation; the Commission found respondents failed to prove non-enablement and the court affirmed.
we discern no error with its conclusion that Respondents failed to prove a lack of enablement.
12332: Enablement of prior art for obviousness purposes; argument forfeited as not raised before the Board and alternatively rejected on the merits.
The arguments are therefore forfeited, given the important principle that strongly precludes faulting the Board for inadequacies not timely and fairly called to its attention.
12345: Enablement of claims 1-4 of the '659 patent; later-existing valsartan-sacubitril complexes cannot be used to show non-enablement; district court's finding of enablement affirmed.
we affirm the district court's determination that MSN failed to show that the claims are invalid for lack of enablement.
12392: Enablement under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) for claims 1, 4-6, 10 and 13 of the '878 application. The Board's affirmance of the Examiner's rejection for lack of enablement of the full scope of the claims was sustained under substantial evidence review.

Based on this record, the Board's factual findings are supported by substantial evidence and we discern no legal error in its determination of lack of enablement for the claims of the '878 Application.
12732: Whether the PAR, as an anticipatory reference, is enabled

Contrary to Sage's accusation, the Board did not consider Degala to fill in gaps in the PAR but, instead, to assess the state of the prior art at the time the patent application was filed, which the Board is permitted to do.
12792: Enablement under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a): the court held the claims invalid because they explicitly cover an inoperable, non-enabled alternative embodiment, affirming the invalidity judgment.

We conclude the claims are invalid for lack of enablement because, to comply with 35 U.S.C. § 112(a)'s enablement requirement, the specification must enable the full scope of the invention as defined by its claims.
13223: Enablement of full scope of asserted method-of-treatment claims; JMOL of no enablement reversed
we conclude that JMOL of no enablement was improper.
14115: Enablement of the claimed enzyme genus under §112(a) in the PGR, including reliance on post-priority-date experimental data to show the claims were not enabled. The Board found claims 1-33 not enabled, and the court affirmed.
The massive disparity between the amount claimed and the amount disclosed supports the Board’s finding of lack of enablement.
14520: Enablement of the full scope of the claims without undue experimentation
No reasonable jury could have found that the specification of the '039 patent teaches a skilled artisan how to make and use the full scope of the claimed invention.
14700: Enablement of asserted claims 1, 3, 9 of '314 patent and claim 1 of '162 patent; district court granted JMOL of invalidity for lack of enablement, affirmed.
We disagree. Wyeth mischaracterizes the district court's analysis, and, regardless, the specification fails to enable the claims as properly construed.
14776: Enablement of claims 20-24 under 35 U.S.C. 112(a); Board affirmed rejection that claims are not enabled (undue experimentation to practice full scope of claimed ribavirin aerosol range).
we affirm the Board's finding that claims 20–24 are not enabled.
